memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"The son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat of the fellowship offering shall have the right thigh as his share. From the fellowship offerings of the Israelites, I have taken the breast that is waved and the thigh that is presented and have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as their perpetual share from the Israelites."'" - Lev 7:33-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
I have taken... and have given them.

Look at the two verbs. God takes the portion from the people, and God gives it to the priests. He puts Himself in the middle of the transaction.

This matters enormously for how both sides understood it. The Israelite was not paying the priest; he was giving to God. And the priest was not receiving from the people; he was receiving from God. Nobody was anyone's employer, and nobody was anyone's dependent.

That arrangement protects relationships. Where money passes directly between people, power follows it. The giver can start to feel ownership; the receiver can start to feel obligation. God deliberately stood between them.

Something of this remains for us. Paul was careful to say of a gift he received, Not that I desire your gifts; what I desire is that more be credited to your account (Phil 4:17). He would not let the Philippians think they had bought his loyalty, and he would not let himself become their servant instead of Christ's.

Give to God, and let Him do the distributing. Receive from God, and thank Him rather than feeling indebted to people.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When I give, do I give to God or to an institution — and does it show in my attitude?
2. Do I let gratitude to God replace unhealthy obligation toward people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You take and You give. Let my giving be to You, and let whatever I receive come to me from Your hand. Amen.
